cards.front: magnet
cards.back: An object that attracts some metals such as iron.
cards.say: magnet. An object that attracts some metals such as iron.

cards.front: magnetic material
cards.back: A material that a magnet attracts. Iron and steel are magnetic.
cards.say: magnetic material. A material that a magnet attracts. Iron and steel are magnetic.

cards.front: Which metal is magnetic, iron or copper?
cards.back: Iron. Copper is not magnetic.
cards.say: Which metal is magnetic, iron or copper? Iron. Copper is not magnetic.

cards.front: Is a steel paper clip magnetic?
cards.back: Yes, because steel contains iron.
cards.say: Is a steel paper clip magnetic? Yes, because steel contains iron.

cards.front: Is a plastic ruler magnetic?
cards.back: No. Plastic is not magnetic.
cards.say: Is a plastic ruler magnetic? No. Plastic is not magnetic.

cards.front: Is an aluminium can magnetic?
cards.back: No. Aluminium is a metal but it is not magnetic.
cards.say: Is an aluminium can magnetic? No. Aluminium is a metal but it is not magnetic.

cards.front: Is a wooden spoon magnetic?
cards.back: No. Wood is not magnetic.
cards.say: Is a wooden spoon magnetic? No. Wood is not magnetic.

cards.front: Do all metals stick to magnets?
cards.back: No. Only some metals, such as iron and steel, are magnetic.
cards.say: Do all metals stick to magnets? No. Only some metals, such as iron and steel, are magnetic.

cards.front: pole
cards.back: One of the two ends of a magnet, where the pull is strongest. Each magnet has a north pole and a south pole.
cards.say: pole. One of the two ends of a magnet, where the pull is strongest. Each magnet has a north pole and a south pole.

cards.front: What happens when two opposite poles meet?
cards.back: They attract. They pull together.
cards.say: What happens when two opposite poles meet? They attract. They pull together.

cards.front: What happens when two like poles meet?
cards.back: They repel. They push apart.
cards.say: What happens when two like poles meet? They repel. They push apart.

cards.front: attract
cards.back: To pull towards.
cards.say: attract. To pull towards.

cards.front: repel
cards.back: To push away.
cards.say: repel. To push away.

cards.front: Where is a magnet strongest?
cards.back: At its poles.
cards.say: Where is a magnet strongest? At its poles.

cards.front: Do magnets need to touch to work?
cards.back: No. A magnet can pull or push without touching, through a gap.
cards.say: Do magnets need to touch to work? No. A magnet can pull or push without touching, through a gap.

cards.front: Can a magnet work through paper?
cards.back: Yes. The pull passes through thin non-magnetic materials.
cards.say: Can a magnet work through paper? Yes. The pull passes through thin non-magnetic materials.

cards.front: How can you test if a material is magnetic?
cards.back: Hold a magnet close to the material and see if it is pulled to it.
cards.say: How can you test if a material is magnetic? Hold a magnet close to the material and see if it is pulled to it.

cards.front: Which pair will push apart, a north and a south pole, or two north poles?
cards.back: Two north poles. Like poles repel.
cards.say: Which pair will push apart, a north and a south pole, or two north poles? Two north poles. Like poles repel.

cards.front: Which pair will pull together, a north and a south pole, or two south poles?
cards.back: A north and a south pole. Opposite poles attract.
cards.say: Which pair will pull together, a north and a south pole, or two south poles? A north and a south pole. Opposite poles attract.

cards.front: Name something that uses magnets.
cards.back: A fridge door, a compass or a magnetic toy.
cards.say: Name something that uses magnets. A fridge door, a compass or a magnetic toy.

cards.front: compass
cards.back: A tool with a magnet needle that points north.
cards.say: compass. A tool with a magnet needle that points north.

cards.front: Why do recycling centres use big magnets?
cards.back: Big magnets lift iron and steel and leave other materials behind.

cards.front: True or false: Magnets attract all materials.
cards.back: False. A magnet only attracts magnetic materials.
